strings.title: Multiplying by Powers of Ten
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Multiplying by 10, 100 or 1000 makes each digit worth 10, 100 or 1000 times as much, so the digits move to the left.
strings.keywords: power of ten, place value, digits move, 10^3
watchFor: "Add a zero" with decimals (3.4 × 10 = 3.40): ask "Is 3.40 ten times as much as 3.4?"
Moving the digits the wrong way: ask "Should the answer be bigger or smaller?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "What happens to the digits when you multiply by 1000?" Land: each digit becomes worth 1000 times as much, moving three places left. "Add a zero" doesn't work for decimals.

problems.notes: Look for: 3 ones become 3 tens, 4 tenths become 4 ones. Ask: "What happened to each digit?" Model: ratio 1:3.4, 10:34

responses.say: Each digit is worth 10 times as much: 34.

responses.tip: "Added a zero." Ask: is 3.40 ten times as much as 3.4?

problems.notes: Look for: 10 × 34. Ask: "How does the last one help?" Model: ratio 1:3.4, 10:34, 100:340
Look for: one more × 10. Ask: "How many places do the digits move?" Model: ratio 1:3.4, 10:34, 100:340, 1000:3400
Look for: 5 tenths become 5 tens. Ask: "Where does the 5 go?" Model: ratio 1:0.56, 100:56

responses.say: 5 tenths become 5 tens, 6 hundredths become 6 ones: 56.

problems.notes: Look for: thousandths become ones. Ask: "What is each digit worth now?" Model: ratio 1:0.072, 1000:72

responses.say: 7 hundredths become 7 tens, 2 thousandths become 2 ones: 72.

responses.tip: Moved two places. Ask: how many zeros in 1000?

problems.notes: Look for: 4 ones become 4 hundreds; 5 thousandths become 5 tenths. Ask: "What about the zeros in the middle?" Model: ratio 1:4.005, 100:400.5

responses.tip: Ask: should the answer be about 400?

problems.notes: Look for: 10^4 = 10 000, digits move 4 places. Ask: "What does the exponent tell you?" Model: ratio 1:0.3, 10000:3000

strings.title: Dividing by Powers of Ten
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Dividing by 10, 100 or 1000 makes each digit worth a tenth, hundredth or thousandth as much, so the digits move to the right.
strings.keywords: power of ten, divide, place value, digits move right
watchFor: "Take off a zero" when there isn't one (34 ÷ 100 = 3.4): ask "Is 3.4 a hundredth of 34?"
Losing place holders (7 ÷ 1000 = 0.7): ask "How many places should the 7 move?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How is dividing by 100 the opposite of multiplying by 100?" Land: the digits move right, one place for each power of ten; use zeros to hold empty places.

problems.notes: Look for: 3 tens become 3 ones. Ask: "What is each digit worth now?" Model: ratio 10:34, 1:3.4
Look for: one more ÷ 10. Ask: "How does the last one help?" Model: ratio 100:34, 10:3.4, 1:0.34
Look for: three places right. Ask: "Where is the 3 now?" Model: ratio 1000:34, 1:0.034
Look for: 5 hundreds become 5 ones. Ask: "Is there a quick way?" Model: ratio 100:560, 1:5.6

responses.tip: Took off one zero. Ask: is that ÷ 10 or ÷ 100?

problems.notes: Look for: 7 ones become 7 thousandths. Ask: "How many zeros hold the places?" Model: ratio 1000:7, 1:0.007
Look for: 4 tens become 4 tenths. Ask: "Where does each digit go?" Model: ratio 100:45.6, 1:0.456
Look for: 10^3 = 1000. Ask: "What does the exponent tell you?" Model: ratio 1000:2, 1:0.002

strings.title: Times 0.1 Is Divide by 10
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Multiplying by 0.1, 0.01 or 0.001 gives the same result as dividing by 10, 100 or 1000.
strings.keywords: tenth of, hundredth of, equivalent, multiply by a decimal
watchFor: Thinking multiplying always makes bigger (50 × 0.1 = 500): ask "What is a tenth of 50?"
Mixing 0.1 and 0.01: ask "Is 0.01 a tenth or a hundredth?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Why is × 0.1 the same as ÷ 10?" Land: 0.1 is one tenth, so × 0.1 finds a tenth of the number: the same as ÷ 10.

problems.notes: Look for: a known fact. Ask: "Hold on to this." Model: text 50 / 10 = 5
Look for: a tenth of 50. Ask: "Why is it the same as the last one?" Word choice: "0.1 of 50 is a tenth of 50." Model: text 50 x 0.1 = 50 / 10 = 5

responses.say: 0.1 is one tenth, so a tenth of 50 is 5.

responses.tip: Ask: is 0.1 more or less than 1? So is the answer more or less than 50?

problems.notes: Look for: a hundredth of 50. Ask: "What's 0.01 as a division?" Model: text 50 x 0.01 = 50 / 100 = 0.5

responses.tip: Ask: is 0.01 a tenth or a hundredth?

problems.notes: Look for: a tenth of 3.6. Ask: "What is each digit worth now?" Model: text 3.6 x 0.1 = 3.6 / 10 = 0.36

responses.tip: Ask: should the answer be bigger or smaller than 3.6?

problems.notes: Look for: same as × 0.01. Ask: "Can you write it as a multiplication?" Model: text 3.6 / 100 = 3.6 x 0.01 = 0.036

responses.tip: That's ÷ 10. Ask: how many places for ÷ 100?

problems.notes: Look for: same as ÷ 1000. Ask: "What's 0.001 as a division?" Model: text 250 x 0.001 = 250 / 1000 = 0.25
Look for: a hundredth of 0.8. Ask: "Do you trust the pattern with a decimal?" Model: text 0.8 x 0.01 = 0.8 / 100 = 0.008

responses.tip: Ask: is that a tenth or a hundredth of 0.8?
